subject: Embed + Rerank + Funcall compatibility summary and next commits
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@brightline.ai>
Cc: ops@brightline.ai; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Post-demo alignment — embedding/rerank + funcalls

Lucy — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next commits so we have alignment. I tried to keep this tight so your ops and eng teams can scan.

Pain points you reiterated
- Search precision drops on long-tail queries (low recall on medical content) — embeddings currently inconsistent across locale-specific content.
- Latency spikes when ranking at query time with the current microservice setup (impacting user experience).
- Need for structured outputs for downstream normalization (entities + confidence) to feed the triage queue.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) Improve candidate recall with a unified embed + rerank pipeline; end-to-end p95 latency for rerank < 250ms for median queries.
2) Add a funcall-enabled rerank step so you can attach provenance and structured entities to top-N results.
3) Production-grade SDK hooks so your engineers can plug into streaming responses and structured outputs without changing your runtime significantly.

What we think is feasible (initial compatibility plan)
- Embedding sync: run a small pilot using Redwood embeddings with locale-aware tokenization; expected delta: +4–7% recall on pilot seed set.
- Rerank with funcalls: attach a lightweight funcall that emits entity JSON for each candidate; Redwood streaming will emit partial tokens while the rerank function finalizes structured output.
- SDK changes: we propose a 2-file addition to your client SDK (embed adapter + rerank callback). No breaking API surface; optional flag to enable funcall-mode.

Immediate next commits (proposed owners and dates)
- Redwood: share SDK patch + test harness by Tue 2027-05-18 (Ben, Sergio).
- Brightline: provide a representative seed query set + sample documents by Thu 2027-05-20 (Lucy / Ops).
- Joint: schedule a 60-min test-run for pilot evaluation the week of 2027-05-24.

Attachments: I attached a short requirements workbook and the SDK change proposal (see attached file names).

If that matches what you heard, I’ll upload the SDK draft to the shared Drive and open a HubSpot task for the pilot. Let me know if you want me to loop in Solutions Eng for a pairing session.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Attachment stubs: brightline-inference-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet), sdk-change-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Lucy Park <lucy.park@brightline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightline.ai
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Post-demo alignment — embedding/rerank + funcalls

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures our discussion. A couple clarifications from ops:
- Seed query set: we’ll include 2 months of anonymized triage queries. Expect to drop PII and redactions. Can you confirm the format you prefer (CSV with doc_id, query_text, label)?
- Latency target: the 250ms p95 is ambitious but acceptable as a pilot target. We need visibility into how batching will affect tail latency.
- Security/compliance: we’ll need a note about how cached KV content is isolated per-tenant (SOC2 requirement).

We’ll aim to get the data package to you by Thu. Also, can Redwood provide a small synthetic run that demonstrates streaming funcalls producing structured JSON (schema example)? That will help our backend team sign off.

—Lucy
Lucy Park | Head of Product
Brightline AI
lucy.park@brightline.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@brightline.ai>, ops@brightline.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Post-demo alignment — embedding/rerank + funcalls

Lucy — nice, thanks. Quick answers inline and next steps.

- Data format: CSV with columns (doc_id, query_text, label, locale) is perfect. If you can include tokenization hints or language tags that helps our embedding pilot.
- Batching and tail latency: our runtime supports workload-aware batching. For the pilot we’ll run unbatched mode for a subset of queries to get baseline latency numbers, then an optimized batched run. We’ll provide a short latency matrix so you can see p50/p95/p99 across modes.
- KV isolation: Redwood Dedicated/Private runs support per-tenant KV namespaces and encrypted caches. I’ll have Sergio attach a short SOC2-friendly note explaining the isolation model.

Deliverables and owners (confirming)
- SDK draft + synthetic demo (streaming funcall → structured JSON): Redwood (Ben + Sergio) — deliver Tue 2027-05-18 EOD.
- Short SOC2 isolation note: Redwood (Sergio) — deliver Mon 2027-05-17 midday.
- Data package (CSV) + preferred sample queries: Brightline (Lucy / Ops) — Thu 2027-05-20.
- Pilot run and results review: joint session week of 2027-05-24 — schedule to follow.

If that looks right I’ll push the SDK patch to the Drive and create the HubSpot task DL-2027-0953 with the checklist.

Ben
